title: Jackie D NDE 4778
content: On the fourth night after major surgery I had a cardiac arrest. One minute I was telling a nurse I had chest pain, the next, my father was in my room, and we were alone. He stood at the left side of the end of my bed, and I must have been talking too much (as I do), because he interrupted me in a slightly impatient voice, by saying, 'Jackie, you have to make up your mind, are you coming or not??' He used a 'tone' that he always used when I wouldn't get up at 5:00 am in the middle of winter to attend swimming training, after begging him the night before to wake me! This was in my primary school age. I 'ummed' and 'arhed' and finally said 'I better not!' Before I could tell him why, he was gone. I was surrounded by doctors and nurses, with one doctor yelling my name. I felt a bit cheated that I didn't experience tunnels, white lights, etc. but also, and continue to feel, a deep sense of satisfaction that our loved ones come to meet us when our time is up. What surprised me most of all was I didn't see any white lights, and surrounding dad was a blackness of a depth of color I've never seen before. I felt very strongly, that everything around him was blacked out so I couldn't see anything surrounding him! I remember feeling frustrated and a bit cheated that I couldn't 'see' anything. I described to my mother a few days later what dad was wearing. Mum was shocked that I described 'a light blue suit, but it wasn't a suit, it didn't have long sleeves - I couldn't quite describe it'??? Mum then informed me she had dressed dad in his favorite suit for the coffin. Apparently it was called a 'safari suit' popular in the 1970's on the Gold Coast. It was then that I remembered him wearing it to work. He died thirty-two years before and I was only twenty-one years old when he passed, so I had no knowledge about such things.

environment.environment_other_detail: A blackness of a depth of color I've never seen before; everything around her father seemed 'blacked out' so she couldn't see anything surrounding him.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Cardiac arrest on the fourth night after major surgery.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: No OBE/tunnel/light described; instead an immediate encounter with her deceased father in a black void-like setting, a question about whether she was 'coming or not,' her decision not to go, and an immediate return to awareness of doctors and nurses.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Encounter consisted mainly of her deceased father appearing in her hospital room/at bedside with surrounding blackness 'blacked out' so she could not see anything else; no tunnel or white light. Father used a familiar impatient tone and asked, 'are you coming or not??' She decided, 'I better not!'
unique_elements.notable_quotes: 'Jackie, you have to make up your mind, are you coming or not??' ; 'I better not!' ; 'a blackness of a depth of color I've never seen before.'
